Status

FinKore Core 2.0.4 stable. This is the shared, language-neutral normative baseline. Stability applies to the defined observable contract and the compatibility policy in Conventions. The domain scope is Money, Workflow, Audit, Approvals, and Entities.

Purpose

The specification defines the observable financial behavior an implementation preserves: values, results, failures, and invariants. You choose the language, API, framework, and storage. CoreDoc states the financial obligations that these domain rules refine.

How to read a specification

Choose a domain below and follow its reading path. Most documents use the same structure:

SectionWhat it tells you
Purpose and terminologyThe problem and the terms used in its rules
RequirementsObligations, recommendations, and permissions, with stable IDs for reference
InvariantsProperties that continue to hold across operations
Examples and invalid examplesConcrete illustrations of the rules
ErrorsPortable failure codes and the conditions that produce them
Open Questions and Non-GoalsUnresolved topics and the limits of the document

Read the normative-language conventions before assessing conformance. They distinguish requirements from explanation and examples. Use the glossary as a reference when a term is unfamiliar; you do not need to read it from beginning to end first.

Organization

DomainStart here when you need to understand…
MoneyExact amounts, currency compatibility, calculations, and rounding
WorkflowPermitted lifecycle changes and rejected transitions
AuditWhat happened, who acted, and how history is preserved
ApprovalsWhich business decisions are required and whether they remain effective
Financial EntitiesStable identity, valid changes, revisions, and evolution over time

Later domain specifications can compose these areas. The rules for explicit refinements are defined by SPEC-TERMINOLOGY-001 in Conventions.

Each domain index links to all of its specification documents. Shared rules for compatibility, stable identifiers, portable values, and errors are in Conventions.

Scope Discipline (Non-Normative)

FinKore Core deliberately begins with reusable primitives rather than concrete invoice, expense, purchase-order, payment, reimbursement, or journal-entry models. Applications may compose the primitives for those domains, but Core 2.0 does not claim to standardize them.

Ledger posting, reconciliation, payments, tax, and concrete correction or reversal accounting effects remain deferred. Domain documents record their specific Open Questions and Non-Goals. New concepts begin with a financial domain problem and specification review; possible future topics are not current commitments.

Conformance

Conformance is defined by SPEC-CONFORMANCE-001 and SPEC-CONFORMANCE-002 in Conventions. Examples illustrate expected behavior but are non-normative unless explicitly identified as normative.

The conformance artifacts connect requirements to portable acceptance cases. The Agentic Contract describes canonical operation semantics for machine clients. Both derive from /spec. The implementation guide explains how to use them in your own codebase.

Version Identity (Non-Normative)

FinKore Core 2.0.4 identifies the compatible patch baseline. The conformance manifest and vector-file formats have separate versions, as do consumer-owned tools and implementations. See the compatibility policy for the portable surface protected by Core stability.

Non-Goals

This specification does not prescribe programming constructs, user interfaces, storage systems, network protocols, or deployment architecture. This repository publishes the contract and maintenance tools; consumers own financial implementations and execution tooling.
